body:
Fixes #2134.

## What went wrong

Issue #2130's task was reported in Telegram as `❌ Work session killed — out of memory or forced kill (SIGKILL) (exit code: 137)` at 17:42:06 UTC, while PR #2131 carried on silently — and the container actually kept working for another 3.5 hours, finished with **exit code 0** at 21:11:07 and auto-merged the pull request. Nothing in the PR ever said a kill had been observed.

Root cause (reconstructed from the raw evidence in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2134`](docs/case-studies/issue-2134/README.md)): the host reached 822 MB free of 12.5 GB, the kernel OOM killer killed a process inside the container, Docker set `State.OOMKilled = true` — and Hive Mind treated that flag as terminal. Docker sets the flag when **any** process in the container cgroup is OOM-killed ([moby/moby#47618](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/47618)), so the container itself was still `running` in the very same polling round.

## What this PR changes

- **The OOM flag is an observation, not a verdict.** The evidence ladder is: log footer → container liveness → kill. Only a dead container with no footer is reported as killed (issue #2015's real kills are preserved).
- **Every kill is diagnosed exactly**, from evidence already being collected: the `📈 [RESOURCES]` markers in the session log, cgroup v2 `memory.events`, `/proc/meminfo`, disk usage and the kernel OOM report. The message says *out of memory* / *disk full* / *forced kill* and names the process the kernel killed, instead of guessing "out of memory or forced kill".
- **A session that survived the event no longer reads as a plain success** — it completes with a `recovered from out of memory` / `recovered from forced kill` warning (en/ru/zh/hi).
- **The pull request gets the same report.** A notice comment carries the cause, the evidence, the on-kill policy and whether a new working session was started. The intermediate working-session log is uploaded alongside it **only when `--attach-logs` is enabled**, exactly as the issue asks.
- **Configurable, identically in Telegram and in `solve`:** `--on-session-kill=report|resume` (env `HIVE_MIND_ON_SESSION_KILL`, default `report` — today's behaviour) and `--session-kill-resume-attempts` (env `HIVE_MIND_SESSION_KILL_RESUME_ATTEMPTS`, default 1). Under `resume`, the killed session is genuinely restarted through the same isolation backend from the last tool session id found in its own log, the new session is tracked like any other, both surfaces name it, and a session stopped on purpose is never restarted.
- **Case study committed** with the raw evidence (status records, container inspect, logs, timeline), the requirement-by-requirement analysis, root causes and the check of existing components.
- **Upstream report filed:** [link-foundation/start#151](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/151) — `$ --status` reports `executed` / `exitCode 137` from the container OOM flag while `docker inspect` still says `running`, with a reproducible example, the workaround used here and a suggested fix.

## How to reproduce the original bug

`docs/case-studies/issue-2134/README.md` reconstructs the timeline from the recorded artefacts; the minimal reproduction is a container whose helper process is OOM-killed while the main process keeps running — `docker inspect` then reports `State.OOMKilled=true` with `State.Running=true`, which is exactly what the status provider fed to the monitor.

## Tests

`tests/test-issue-2134-killed-session-recovery.mjs` — 86 assertions, all passing, covering:

1. the OOM ladder (live container → not killed; footer `exit 0` → executed; dead + no footer → killed);
2. end-to-end through `monitorSessions()`: no announcement while the container lives, then a single completion carrying the recovery warning, the diagnostics and a PR comment;
3. the exact kill cause (OOM / disk / forced kill) and both kernel OOM-report formats;
4. the PR notice and `--attach-logs` gating (nothing uploaded when disabled);
5. policy resolution from flag and environment, in both surfaces;
6. a killed session under `--on-session-kill=resume` starting exactly **one** recovery session — none under `report`, none once the attempt cap is spent, none after a user stop, none without a real tool session id — and both surfaces naming it;
7. `${sessionId}` and friends never being offered as a resume id.

Full suite: **374/374 test files pass**; `npm run lint` is clean.

## Still open (tracked separately)

A terminal report is never revisited once tracking stops, and `monitorSessions()` is not re-entrancy-guarded (`session_completed` fired three times in this incident). Neither is part of this incident's report path; both are recorded in the case study.

commits.messageBody:
Docker sets `State.OOMKilled` when *any* process in the container cgroup is
OOM-killed, so a container whose helper process died keeps running and can
still exit 0 (moby/moby#47618). Hive Mind treated the flag as terminal, so
session 30920087 was announced as killed at 17:42 while it went on working
until 21:11 and merged its pull request.

The flag is now an observation, not a verdict: the log footer wins, then
container liveness, and only a dead container with no footer is reported as
OOM-killed - which keeps issue #2015's behaviour. The observation is
persisted so the completion can warn that the session recovered from it.

Also stop offering an unexpanded \${sessionId} placeholder as a resume id.

Refs #2134
commits.messageHeadline: fix(2134): verify a container OOM flag before reporting a killed session

commits.messageBody:
…=resume

The option was registered, documented and policy-tested, but nothing in
src/ ever called shouldResumeKilledSession() — so `resume` behaved exactly
like `report` and the documented behaviour was a lie.

The monitor now recovers a confirmed kill before it builds the completion
message, so Telegram and the pull-request notice name the very same new
working session. The recovery session resumes the last tool session id
found in the killed session's own log, runs through the same isolation
backend, and is tracked like any other session; the attempt counter is
carried forward and persisted so --session-kill-resume-attempts (default
1) bounds a job that reliably runs the host out of memory. A session the
user stopped on purpose is never restarted.

title: Better handling of killed task
